title: Split the c=1 sign characters that g and t move
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

For the pinned 8-by-112 centre query, the signed coordinate-permutation stabilizer of sector `c = 1` has order **3072**: 96 permutations, each with 32 sign patterns. On every sign character moved by the predecessor involutions `g` and `t`, an explicit element of that stabilizer splits the character.

The moved characters are four of dimension 432, six of dimension 192, and four of dimension 80. The order-4 permutation `s = (0 4 3 7)(5 6)`, all signs `+1`, has complex eigenvalue multiplicities

- `144, 84, 120, 84` on each 432-dimensional moved character,
- `48, 48, 48, 48` on each 192-dimensional moved character,
- `32, 12, 24, 12` on each 80-dimensional moved character,

for eigenvalues `1, i, -1, -i`. Conjugates in the stabilizer carry these splits onto every moved character of the same dimension. Preserving involutions give the coarser real splits `264 + 168`, `96 + 96` or `120 + 72`, and `56 + 24`. On each character preserved by `s`, the 64 residual elements that preserve the character and commute with `s` act by scalar fourth roots of unity on those eigenspaces.

This is an exhaustive finite census with exact intertwining identities, scoped to signed coordinate permutations of the eight query coordinates whose port map is linear, dot-product orthogonal, and fixes sector 1. It is not a minimal polynomial, not an irreducibility theorem, and not a multiplication bound. Selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`. This draft is based on fork branch `cursor/upstream-7c49fe32-pin-20de`, which is that commit, so the diff is only `research/centre-c1-moved-sign-split/`. Head `fbb3c3f5651dc5871bacdd6e897340514de3297a`.

Task card `formal-interface-lemma`. Scope status: **changed**. The card asks for a formal caller binding. [Discussion comment 19144258](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19144258) asks whether the residual stabilizer of `c = 1` splits its largest sign-character space. [PR #6944](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6944) and discussion comment 19492873 answer that for the characters `g` and `t` preserve. This package answers the remaining `c = 1` clause: the fourteen characters those involutions move. It does not add a Lean binding.

The query is the frozen interface used by `research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/`, SHA256 `5c6c51fbffc07a683e922f17532fd90262ae9e23cc3560a696002073dd234ef3`.

`scripts/find_overlap.py --refresh` on 2026-11-10 covered 8919 of 8917 local notes (complete), 895 open PRs (pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T02:30:38Z), and 6941 discussion records (pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T02:31:38Z). The phrases `432-coordinate` and `sign stabilizer` match the source handoff, comment 19492873, and PR #6944. No other open PR treats the moved-character split. Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, task metadata, and the ledger only. No code diffs were searched.

This is a scoped side result on the historical centre Gram. The degree-881 one-slot polynomial in `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` is unchanged.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only. Both registered modes passed:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-c1-moved-sign-split
```

Marker `PASS_C1_MOVED_SIGN_SPLIT` in normal mode and under `python3 -I -B -O -W error`. Metadata check: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Selected-baseline orientation: `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

The census scans every tetrad automorphism and every sign pattern whose basis image fixes sector 1, checks group closure of all 3072 elements, and enumerates every character-preserving element of one character per moved dimension. Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, a swapped port label, a truncated sign stabilizer, and the sign patterns on `s` that fall outside the stabilizer.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, the degree-410 minor, the selected cold replay, a `c = 3` census, and any basis of a 48-dimensional eigenspace. The centralizer scalar conclusion uses the triangle inequality for unitary roots of unity; the traces themselves are exact integers.

## Credit

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions and the open decomposition question in discussion comment 19144258. The preserved-character split and the operators `g` and `t` are the census in discussion comment 19492873 and PR #6944, by unpaidmoon. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. Krzysztof Wojt's PR5168 is the degree-881 one-slot annihilator. The doubled representation comes from PR1719. New work is Apache-2.0.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. The assistant derived the stabilizer census and wrote the verifier. This is not an independent human or proof-kernel review.

## Open next questions

Recorded in `research/centre-c1-moved-sign-split/TASK.json`.

- Can one element of the `c = 1` stabilizer that preserves a moved 192-character, and does not commute with `s`, meet a 48-dimensional eigenspace of `s` in a smaller `A_1`-invariant subspace? The centralizer acts by scalars, so any finer split has to come from outside it. The trace formula does not list a basis.
- What is the characteristic polynomial of one of those 48-dimensional eigenspaces? It would place the split inside the known degree-881 polynomial. This is separate from the 216-dimensional block left open by PR #6944.
- Which residual signed permutations split the `c = 3` characters? `g` sends sector 3 to 343, so the stabilizer certified here does not act on that block.
